title: Therapeutic Drug Concentration Verification
real_world_story: A hospital's automated prescription validation engine interfaces with a certified clinical pharmacovigilance database. The database maintains a strictly increasing sorted list of N approved therapeutic blood serum concentration thresholds (measured in mg/L). When an electronic prescription is entered, the clinical engine issues Q queries, each inquiring whether an exact target concentration X is present in the certified list. If X is present, the engine outputs its 1-based index in the approved registry; if not, it outputs -1 so that a clinical pharmacist is flagged for manual review.
problem_statement: Given a strictly sorted array of N distinct integers and Q query values X, determine for each query whether X exists in the array. If it does, output its 1-based index; otherwise, output -1.
task: For each of the Q query values, find its 1-based position using logarithmic search, or output -1 if absent.
input_format:
The first line contains two space-separated integers N and Q.
The second line contains N strictly increasing space-separated integers representing the certified concentration levels.
The next Q lines each contain a single integer X representing a query concentration.
output_format: For each query, print its 1-based index in the array on a separate line, or print -1 if the value is not present.

examples.explanation: Query 38 is present at 1-based index 3. Query 10 is not present in the array, so -1 is printed. Query 80 is present at 1-based index 5.
Query 250 does not exist in the array, outputting -1.

real_world_takeaway: Binary search provides predictable O(log N) lookup latency across sorted pharmacological safety databases, enabling real-time clinical decision validation.
